english.title: Knowingly hold another person in slavery / servitude
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) held another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OTHER PERSON..), in slavery or servitude in circumstances, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CIRCUMSTANCES..), when you knew or ought to have known that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was so held
english.legislation: Contrary to section 71(1)(a) and (3) of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
held another person in slavery / servitude
in circumstances when you knew / ought to have known that he/she was so held

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: References to holding a person in slavery or servitude are to be construed in accordance with Article 4 of the Human Rights Convention (which prohibits a person from being held in slavery or servitude).

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit on Prosecutions:
None.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
